content.hook: You don't need pricey gear. You need a system.

slides.title: Start with the *pad*
slides.body: The ground steals warmth. Insulation underneath matters as much as the bag on top.

slides.title: Match the bag to the *night*
slides.body: Plan for the coldest night you expect, not the daytime average. Add a little margin.

slides.title: Keep it *dry*
slides.body: Pack sleeping gear in a waterproof bag. Keep one dry sleep layer that you never ride in.

slides.title: Pack for the *conditions*
slides.body: Enter heat, wind and rain per segment. Gear suggestions adapt to what you set.

content.caption:
Bikepacking sleep system basics: you don't need the priciest kit, you need pieces that work together.

1. Pad first. The ground steals warmth, so insulation underneath matters as much as the bag.
2. Choose your bag for the coldest night you expect, with a little margin.
3. Keep sleeping gear in a waterproof bag, plus one dry layer you never ride in.
4. Let the conditions guide the rest. In BikepackPilot you set surface, heat, wind and rain for each segment, and gear recommendations adapt.

Save this for your next packing session.
